title: Spotlight: TCL CSOT - leading OLED and LCD maker, and inkjet printing pioneer
content: TCL CSOT is one of the world's largest display makers, and one of the leaders in OLED production. TCL CSOT is also the only display maker betting its next-generation OLED capacity almost entirely on inkjet printing rather than evaporation.

title: Kopin receives a $2.4 million OLED microdisplay order from an international thermal weapon sight producer
content: US-based microdisplay developer Kopin Corporation has received a $2.4 million OLED microdisplay order from a leading international thermal weapon sight manufacturer. Kopin says that these OLED displays will be integrated into a next‑generation thermal weapon sight program, enhancing situational awareness and operational performance for end users.

title: AI servers push Asus' August revenue up 51%
content: Asus reported consolidated revenue of NT$94.96 billion (US$3.02 billion) in August 2026, up 12.87% from July and 51.17% from a year earlier — the second-highest monthly figure in company history. Revenue for the first eight months reached NT$645.19 billion (US$20.5 billion), up 42.3% year over year. The company attributed the gain to AI server and PC demand, with motherboard orders also recovering.

title: OpenAI's deeper Samsung tie-up lands on a foundry that is running out of capacity
content: For Samsung Electronics' two loss-making logic businesses, OpenAI's declaration that it is jointly producing and researching next-generation chips with the Korean company matters less as a new logo on the customer list than as a sign of where Samsung's advanced wafers actually go.

title: Enterprise AI spending gives Taiwan's Systex a new growth wing
content: Systex reported consolidated revenue of NT$5.9 billion (approximately US$187 million) in August 2026, up 61.91% from NT$3.64 billion a year earlier. Revenue for the first eight months reached NT$38.01 billion, rising 39.65% from NT$27.22 billion in the same period of 2025. Both monthly and cumulative revenue hit record highs for their respective periods.

title: Jin Lian Cheng expands into semiconductor wafer fab UPS battery recycling
content: Jin Lian Cheng Resources completed an upgrade to its desulfurization production line as demand increased for lead-acid battery recycling tied to high-spec uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems used by semiconductor plants. The Taiwanese waste lead-acid battery processor said the upgrade restored normal operations while improving sulfur oxide treatment, real-time monitoring, and environmental management.

title: Ledlink Optics posts 21-month revenue high on AI server, auto demand
content: Ledlink Optics reported that August revenue climbed on stronger AI server and automotive demand, with consolidated revenue reaching NT$134 million. The figure rose 3.21% from July and 20.42% from a year earlier, as the Taiwan-based supplier said both businesses supported growth heading into the second half of the year.

title: China expands OLED capacity, challenging South Korea in IT and automotive display markets
content: South Korea's long-standing dominance in the global display market is facing an aggressive challenge as major Chinese panel makers—including BOE, China Star Optoelectronics Technology (CSOT), and Visionox—rapidly expand their organic light-emitting diode (OLED) production capacity. title: Getac sees growing drone orders, with 2027 revenue contribution reaching up to 12%
content: Getac Holdings is expanding aggressively into drone opportunities on the back of its strong industrial rugged computer foundation, making the segment a continued growth driver in the second half of 2026.

title: Realtek expands cloud AI push with ASIC and SSD chips
content: Realtek chairman Sun-Chien Chiu, who received an honorary fellowship from Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) this week, said in a public interview that the company is already generating revenue from ASIC projects and has started expanding into 3nm products. Although Realtek's ASIC business is still far smaller than MediaTek's, Chiu said it will continue to grow as more projects come in.

title: Verizon, Corning strike multi-billion-dollar fiber deal for broadband and AI buildout
content: Verizon and Corning have agreed to a multi-billion-dollar supply deal that could shape broadband access and artificial intelligence infrastructure well beyond the US. The pact underscores how telecom networks are becoming a shared foundation for consumer internet, enterprise connectivity, and the data-heavy systems driving the next wave of AI services.
